title: A window-corrected rate search finds no excess change in the 28 listed HD 139139 dips
abstract: We test the 28 published HD 139139 dip times for a change in detected event rate during K2 Campaign 15. A cadence-window map gives 87.039 days of exposure. A likelihood-ratio search over the middle 70 percent of exposure gives p = 0.984 in 100,000 conditional uniform simulations. Distribution and longest-gap tests give p = 0.905 and 0.959. Elapsed-time, quality-window and suspect-event checks retain the null result. Equal-exposure halves contain 14 events each. The fixed-split later-to-early rate ratio has an exact 95 percent interval of 0.442 to 2.263 under independent Poisson detections. Simulated midpoint rate increases of two and five have detection power 0.277 and 0.899. Thus the data do not require a rate change, but moderate changes can be missed. The original visual selection and finite-width event visibility are not calibrated. We find no new dip, object or physical cause. Code, coarse aggregate evidence, a figure, exact input hashes and external retrieval steps are included. Source records remain outside the baseline package.
